com.esignal.jstandard.managers

Interface QuoteManager

  • All Superinterfaces:
    ResourceManager
    All Known Subinterfaces:
    TriggeredQuoteEventManager

    public interface QuoteManager
extends ResourceManager
    Purpose of this class is to provide resources of Quotes.

    QuoteManager allows users to subscribe and unsubscribe to the eSignal symbols. The users are required to pass in a listener for each symbol they subscribe to. All the Quote updates are sent to the listener for that symbol. In this way, multiple listeners can be attached for the same symbol by calling subscribe method multiple times with different QuoteListener. After a successful subscribe the listeners will start listening to the streaming quotes, the updated Quote information can be retrieved using the QuoteEvent fired with new data. We will run through a simple usage of QuoteManager.

    Let's create a factory first. The getFactory() method will retrieves the default implementation of the Factory. The implementation can be changed by calling other getFactory(...) methods OR overriding property "jstandard.resourcemanagerfactory.name" in jstandard.properties. ResourceManagerFactory factory = ResourceManagerFactory.getFactory();

    Now create a QuoteManager using the factory. QuoteManager quoteManager = factory.createQuoteManager();

    To start the connection we now need to create instances of ConnectionSettings and ConnectionListener. (Implement MyConnectionListener) ConnectionSettings myConnectionSettings = new ConnectionSettings("myhost", "myusername", "mypassword"); //If proxy settings are required //myConnectionSettings.setProxyInfo("phost", pport, "puser", "ppass"); ConnectionListener myConnectionListener = new MyConnectionListener(); quoteManager.connect(myConnectionSettings, myConnectionListener); At the start the connection listener will receive an event of connecting and after successful connection connected event.

    To start receiving updates for the symbol, let's subscribe to the QuoteManager with "AAPL" symbol. But before that we also need to have an implementation of the QuoteListener. Let's say we have two listeners: LoggerQuoteListener and MyQuoteListener. QuoteListener loggerQuoteListener = new LoggerQuoteListener(); QuoteListener myQuoteListener = new MyQuoteListener(); quoteManager.subscribe("AAPL", loggerQuoteListener); quoteManager.subscribe("AAPL", myQuoteListener); Now both the listeners will start receiving the updates on the same quote AAPL.

    To receive the updated data please implement QuoteListener's onUpdate method. From QuoteEvent get the Quote object which could have one or more updated fields. There are two ways to read the field's values:

    • Call Iterator.next() after calling Quote.iterator() (preferred). Always call Iterator.hasNext() prior to calling Iterator.next().
    • Call Quote.getFieldItem(short) for each fieldId you are interested in. Always call Quote.isFieldItemNull(short) prior to calling Quote.getFieldItem(short).
    Both methods return a Quote.FieldItem. A Quote.FieldItem is composed of an Id, format and value. The JStandard Field Mappings page of https://developer.theice.com contains mappings of Field Id to LRT. These values are also defined as constants in Quote.FieldItem and are included in the Quote.FieldItem javadoc. Example, Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_BID is integer 20. Use these constants in your code to make your code more readable. New codes may be added in the future. The Quote.FieldItem methods allow the API user to access one or more field values using FieldItem.getValue* methods. Each field is uniquely identified by it's ID and format which should be cross referenced with meta data on the customer portal. See following examples: fieldId=1 means LRT_TYPE_CATEGORY and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.BYTE, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsChar() will return 'char' value. fieldId=13 means LRT_TYPE_SYMBOL and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.STRING, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsString() will return 'String' value. fieldId=50 means LRT_TYPE_52WEEKHIGH and has value in the format of FIELDFORMAT.DOUBLE, thus calling Quote.FieldItem.getValueAsDouble() will return 'double' value. Note that the Quote.iterator() is implicit in the for loop below. 
     
        public void onUpdate(QuoteEvent event) {
                try {
                        for (Quote.FieldItem item : quote) {
                                switch (item.getId()) {
                                case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_CATEGORY: // 1
                                        final char categoryCode = item.getValueAsChar();
                                        System.out.println("CATEGORY CODE value:" + categoryCode);
                                        break;
                                case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_SYMBOL: // 13
                                        final String symbol = item.getValueAsString();
                                        System.out.println("SYMBOL value:" + symbol);
                                        break;
                                case Quote.FieldItem.LRT_TYPE_52WEEKHIGH: // 50
                                        final double high52Week = item.getValueAsDouble();
                                        System.out.println("HIGH52WEEK value:" + high52Week);
                                        break;
                                default:
                                        System.out.println("Default value:" + item.getValue());
                                }
                        }
                } catch (Exception e) {
                        e.printStackTrace();
                }
        }

    Let's say we decide to unsubscribe from the LoggerQuoteListener for the symbol AAPL. Use the same instance that was created while subscribing. quoteManager.unsubscribe("AAPL", loggerQuoteListener); Now only myQuoteListener will receive updates for the quote AAPL.

    Disconnect from the manager in the end. quoteManager.disconnect(); Since we did not unsubscribe for myQuoteListener, calling disconnect will make sure appropriate calls are made before closing the connection.

    01-001-0007

      • subscribe

        void subscribe(java.lang.String symbol,
               QuoteListener quoteListener)
        This method subscribes the given symbol and sends updates to the given QuoteListener. If subscribing to a continuation/forward symbol, you need to call ResourceManager.connect() with ConnectionSettings with flags set as ConnectionFlags.CONNECTION_FLAGS#DBCAPI_FLAG_EXPAND_DISPLAY_KEY.
        Parameters:
        symbol - Symbol value
        quoteListener - QuoteListener value
        See Also:
        QuoteListener

      • subscribeChain

        void subscribeChain(java.lang.String symbol,
                    QuoteListener quoteListener,
                    QuoteRequest quoteRequest)
        This method will subscribe to all the symbols for which a QuoteRequest was made. So, if a response returns back 1000 symbols then the application will be subscribed to all those symbols for the given QuoteListener. Thus it is generally recommended for clients to make "request" with the same information and then pick/choose the symbols that the user would be interested in and then subscribe only on them. It is almost also mandatory to use at least one of the Filters before subscribing to the whole chain.
        Parameters:
        symbol - eSignal Symbol to make a request for.
        quoteListener - Instance of QuoteListener on which all of the symbols will be subscribed.
        quoteRequest - QuoteRequest which will contain request settings like filters.

      • unsubscribeChain

        void unsubscribeChain(java.lang.String symbol,
                      QuoteListener quoteListener,
                      QuoteRequest quoteRequest)
        This method will unsubscribe to all the symbols for which a QuoteRequest was made. So, if a response returns back 1000 symbols then the application will be unsubscribed to all those symbols for the given QuoteListener. interested in and then subscribe only on them.
        Parameters:
        symbol - eSignal Symbol to make a request for.
        quoteListener - Instance of QuoteListener on which all of the symbols will be unsubscribed.
        quoteRequest - QuoteRequest which will contain request settings like filters.

      • request

        void request(java.lang.String[] symbols,
             QuoteRequestListener quoteRequestListener,
             QuoteRequest quoteRequest)
        Purpose of this method is to get a snapshot quote(s) for given array of symbols. Please note this functionality is only available in the LightWeight implementation and not available in the DBC implementation. If you call this method while using the DBC implementation you will receive a NotSupportedException
        Parameters:
        symbols - Array of eSignal Symbol to make a request for.
        quoteRequestListener - Instance of QuoteRequestListener on which the response will be updated.
        quoteRequest - QuoteRequest which will contain additional request information than symbols.

      • requestStockOptionRoots

        void requestStockOptionRoots(java.lang.String symbol,
                             StockOptionRootsListener stockOptionRootsListener)
        Purpose of this method is to return Roots of the given Stock Option symbol. This is important to know for Stocks which could potentially have hundreds of Stock Option Roots. e.g. BAC has O:BAC and O:BAC1 roots.
        Parameters:
        symbol - eSignal Symbol to make a request for.
        stockOptionRootsListener - Instance which will process Stock Option Roots

      • requestOptionMonths

      • keyLookup

        void keyLookup(java.lang.String key,
               LOOKUPTYPE lookupType,
               QuoteKeyListener quoteKeyListener)
        Purpose of this method is to return one/more symbols for a given key. The key could be one of the symbol types defined as LOOKUPTYPE. The QuoteKeyListener will be registered to receive the responses back in the String array format.
        Parameters:
        key - Value of the symbol key type being requested
        lookupType - Type of the key/symbol for which the request is being made. e.g. CUSIP
        quoteKeyListener - Instance which will process the array of symbols.
